senses.gloss: (b. h.) pr. n. m. Eliyahu, Elijah, the great prophet in the days of Ahab, freq. represented, in Talmud and Midrashim, as intervening in behalf of the pious and punishing wrong-doers, and expected, in the Messianic days, to clear up doubts and prepare the heavenly kingdom; cmp.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 58a:13">Ber. 58ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אתא א׳ אידמי ליה וכ׳</he> E. came and appeared to him in the disguise of &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33:3">Gen. R. s. 33</cite>, a. fr. <he>אתא א׳ זכור לטוב</he> E., whose memory be blessed, came &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 1:8">B. Mets. I, 8</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 37a:7">37ᵃ</cite>), a. fr. <he>יהא מונח עד שיבוא א׳</he> let it be deposited until E. shall come (and decide to whom it belongs, i.e. an indefinite time until the matter be cleared up).
Men. 45ᵃ; a. fr.—סֵדֶר אֵלִיָהוּ־ Seder Eliyahu, name of a lost Talmudic treatise, divided into Seder Eliyahu Rabba (Large) and S. E. Zuta (Small).
